absent: Numeric values and widths of capacity, period, ceiling, divider, time quantum, skip threshold and validity marker constants.
Complete field lists, sizes, alignment and padding of averaging, runqueue, fair queue, entity and group structures.
Contracts and side effects of sum aging, entity aging, queue PELT clock, processor capacity scaling, migration lag compensation, weight scaling and time reading helpers not routed here.
Lock ordering across runqueue, fair queue removal and bandwidth locks plus interrupt and preemption context requirements.
Utilization estimation maintenance and throttle distribution with unthrottle transitions for PELT clocks.
Trace payload contents and frequency control callback contracts.

findings.text: Load decay treats very large period gaps as fully decayed to an empty value, otherwise folds whole periods into halving shifts and applies a table factor for the remainder, giving bounded constant time behavior independent of gap size.

Segment accumulation combines a decayed opening portion, a middle contribution derived from the ceiling value minus its decayed form minus a unit, and a closing portion that needs no decay, yielding the total for a multi period span.
The normalization divisor is a fixed minimum plus the current partial period contribution carried by the averaging state, so recent partial progress increases the denominator.

Average refresh divides accumulated sums by the current divisor, weighting the load term by caller supplied load while runnable and utilization terms use their sums directly, with utilization published by single copy store.
Capacity scaling multiplies a time or value by a capacity factor and normalizes by a fixed shift, preserving proportionality across heterogeneous capacities.

Runqueue PELT time advance delegates idle runqueues to a synchronization path, while busy runqueues scale the elapsed interval by processor and frequency capacities before advancing the PELT clock, acknowledging that slower execution borrows idle time that later idle synchronization repays.
Idle synchronization aligns the PELT clock with the task clock and records wall and PELT idle snapshots through tearing safe stores separated by an ordering barrier.
Reading PELT time produces the stored PELT clock less a lost idle correction, and is only valid when the runqueue lock is held and clocks are fresh.
Runqueue wall, task and PELT time readers each assert that the runqueue lock is held and that clocks were updated since the last pin, warning on a single occasion when updates were skipped.

Lock address selection has two builds, one choosing a shared core lock when core scheduling is enabled and a private lock otherwise, and a simpler build always choosing the private lock, with context annotations aliasing the result.

Queue and entity navigation adapts to group scheduling builds, following direct parent and group queue links or deriving the queue from the task and processor, with group lookup producing absence in non group builds and task lookup warning when applied to non tasks in one variant.
Frequency capacity has a default implementation reporting full scale, and interrupt load aging has a trivial build that reports no update.
Averaging accumulation adds signed deltas to both average and sum with negative saturation and enforces that each sum stays at least the average scaled by the minimum divider.

Load refresh covers entity aging unless skipped, queue refresh with pending group propagation, migration attach versus departure detach with group refresh versus decay notification with optional group refresh, plus optional utilization estimation.
Entity attachment synchronizes aging with a feature gated choice between full aging and skipped aging, and folds load, refreshes group share, and propagates upward.

Load attachment aligns entity timestamps and partial contribution with its queue, rebuilds entity sums from averages under the new divisor with weight normalization and unity floor, folds entity values into queue totals, and flags upward propagation with utilization notification.
Load detachment removes entity utilization, runnable and weighted load contributions from the queue and records a negative propagation amount, accompanied by utilization notification.

Group share refresh skips the root group and offline processors, limits work to millisecond granularity, and only publishes load and runnable deltas by atomic addition when either delta exceeds a sixty fourth of its last contribution, recording new contributions and time.

Group propagation is inert for tasks and for queues without a pending flag, otherwise it clears the flag on a single occasion, chains the pending runnable amount upward, and refreshes parent utilization, runnable and load views.

Parent refresh copies child utilization and runnable averages and rescales their sums to the parent divisor, while load refresh folds signed pending runnable with ceiling clipping for additions, equal share estimation for removals without inflating the entity, and a floor at the running portion before weight scaling.

Queue refresh drains stashed removed averages under a dedicated lock, subtracts them scaled by the current divisor, records a corresponding negative propagation amount, ages the queue and snapshots its update time with a tearing safe store, reporting whether any decay occurred.
Queue aging feeds scaled weight, hierarchical runnable count and current presence into sum aging, and on change renormalizes averages and signals decay.

Throttle synchronization does nothing without bandwidth control, at the root, or in the disabled build, otherwise it inherits the parent throttle count, snapshots PELT time, and marks the PELT clock throttled whenever the inherited count is nonzero so that later enqueue or distribution can clear it.
Utilization change notification forwards to frequency control only for the root fair queue of a runqueue.
Frequency utilization update dereferences a per processor callback under scheduler read protection and invokes it with current runqueue time when present, with an alternate build that does nothing.
Interrupt time reading retries around a sequence counter until a consistent total is observed, and enablement is a static branch predicate or a constant false in the disabled build.
Extended scheduler clock publication does nothing when the feature is off or in the disabled build, otherwise it stores the clock and sets a valid marker with release ordering.

Feature queries and group helpers have dual builds, reading a static branch or a control bitmask for features, and recording propagation and refreshing group shares or compiling to empty operations when group support is absent.

Averaging state carries paired average and sum values for load, utilization and runnable behavior plus a partial period contribution and a last update timestamp, with attach aligning timestamps and rebuilding sums under the queue divisor.

Runqueue state holds PELT, task and wall clocks with lost idle correction and idle snapshots, processor identity, current task, and locking, while fair queue state holds averaging state, load weight, runnable and hierarchical counts, current marker, stashed removals with lock, propagation flags and amounts, group contribution snapshots, and throttle markers.

Sixty four bit times use a plain store on wide builds but a value plus ordered copy pair on narrow builds, idle synchronization pairs its ordering barrier with a reader barrier elsewhere, and extended scheduler validity uses release ordering.
Attachment rescaling is explicitly approximate truncation while outside the hierarchy, and load sum normalization divides by entity weight with a unity floor to avoid collapse to an empty value.

The utilization signal excludes idle execution because idle belongs to another class and excludes non fair execution such as real time, may miss boundary transitions but relies on frequent invocation, and needs architecture frequency scaling for invariance.
Decay bounds the gap to avoid excessive shifting, producing an empty value beyond a multiple of the period, and safely narrows to thirty two bits before period folding.
Referenced symbolic constants include capacity shift and scale, load averaging period and ceiling, and minimum divider.

Referenced symbolic controls include a millisecond quantum for group refresh, a clock skip threshold, an extended scheduler valid marker, and action flags for skipping aging, attaching, detaching, group refresh and utilization estimation.
Small runqueue and entity helpers expose processor identity, scaled entity weight, and task to runqueue mapping for use by load and clock paths.
Default frequency capacity scaling is provided as a globally visible routine reporting full scale so platforms without special handling link successfully.
